component.name: CPU Turbo
component.summary: Toggle Intel turbo and cool the laptop from the tray

description.p: Problem: Ubuntu laptops with Intel turbo, a discrete NVIDIA GPU, and background container VMs run hot and loud even when you are barely using them. Boost clocks, the Performance power profile, Docker Desktop’s VM, and NVIDIA drawing the screen all dump heat into the chassis. The palm rest gets uncomfortable, fans spin up, and the usual fixes are scattered across Settings, the terminal, and a logout — so people leave everything on and the machine stays warm.

Solution: CPU Turbo puts the heat switches in one system-tray flyout. Turn Intel turbo off, drop to a cooler battery profile, stop the container VM, and pick Intel or on-demand graphics instead of NVIDIA. The panel shows CPU and internal chassis-sensor temperature, a live report, and a countdown so you can see whether the laptop is actually cooling. Built by BinaryPlates (Mohammad Mustafa) for Ubuntu laptops. https://blazorplate.net
